To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the major risk factors for criminal conduct are: (a) antisocial attitudes, (b) association with antisocial peers, (c) antisocial personality pattern, (d) substance abuse, and (e) family, school, work, leisure, and neighborhood factors that support antisocial behavior.

(a) the most important risk factors for criminal conduct are antisocial personality pattern, antisocial associates and attitudes, family, school and work history, and neighborhood; (b) the most important protective factors for crime are the opposite of the risk factors, and also include substance abuse, mental disorder, and the absence of a stable marriage; (c) the most important needs for rehabilitation are to change antisocial personality pattern through treatment and to change the social context of the person through community intervention;
the major risk/need factors are the major determinants of criminal conduct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general personality and social psychology of criminal conduct, a psychology of criminal conduct that is based upon the integration of theory, empirical research, and practice.
the development of a comprehensive theory of criminal conduct that is consistent with the scientific evidence.

the development of a comprehensive personality theory of criminal conduct, one that is consistent with the empirical data and that provides the basis for a general theory of crime prevention and treatment of offenders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the general personality and social psychology of criminal conduct is an integrated and comprehensive model of the causes, prevention, treatment, and classification of criminal conduct.
the PCC model of criminal behavior, and especially the PIC R perspective, provides a comprehensive and empirically supported theory of the causes and prevention of criminal conduct.

a psychology of criminal conduct is possible, that the RNR model provides a useful framework to guide its development, that a general personality and social psychology approach provides a useful theoretical context for its development and integration, and that a number of major risk/need factors and strengths have been identified and can be used to guide assessment, prevention, and rehabilitation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
criminal conduct is a product of the interaction of the individual, the individual's social environment, and the individual's physical environment.

the major causes of criminal behavior are the interaction of a person with a set of personal, interpersonal, and community factors that, over time, produce the development of a persistent pattern of antisocial behavior.
the Psychology of CriminalConduct (PCC) is a general personality and social psychological perspective that isbased in a general social learning theory of human behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the most effective approach to the prevention and control of criminal behavior is to understand the person and the social context in which the person operates and the interaction of the person with the social context.
the most important thing is not to get caught. If you get caught, you are going to get punished, and if you don't get caught, you will be rewarded.
the psychology of criminal conduct is not a simple matter of individual pathology or social context.
